claim: If positive sector weights g_k approximate positive target weights f_k pointwise within relative error delta, then reweighting both by any supplied nonnegative rational likelihood table preserves normalized joint distributions within TV at most delta/(1-delta), independently of event mass.
quantifiers: Finite sector set k=0,...,N; finite outcome set T; f_k>0; 0<delta<1; (1-delta)f_k<=g_k<=(1+delta)f_k; h(k,t)>=0 with at least one positive entry.
proof: For r_k=g_k/f_k and R=Z'/Z=E_P[r_k], R is in [1-delta,1+delta]. On common support Q/P=r_k/R. The maximum possible ratio deviation gives TV(P,Q)<=delta/(1-delta). Full proof in RESULT.txt §2.
cost: For each explicit f_k=exp(-(k-N/2)^2/N), the direct rational Taylor/range-reduction construction uses r_k=O(N), m_k=O(1+log(N/delta)), and produces g_k with O(N m_k(log N+log m_k)) bits; all N+1 weights are constructed in deterministic time polynomial in N and the encoded rational delta. Normalization and a K-category CDF use polynomial-bit rational arithmetic; a dyadic grid uses O(log(K/gamma)) bits. Exact output and intermediate bit sizes are included.
source_boundary: The composition lemma is independent of Chen-Liu and Cycle-3. The explicit target weights are directly approximable in polynomial bit time, so neither N125 nor a sector-mixture oracle removes a representation/acquisition barrier here. The direct construction is internally proved; it is not a novelty claim.
falsifier: A rational finite table violating the TV inequality under the stated common-support assumptions.
evidence: verify_consumer_gate.py exact Fraction fixture; this is finite corroboration, not the general proof.

claim: If positive rational Dicke-sector weights g_k satisfy a<=g_k/f_k<=b, normalization yields a full-space Loewner sandwich with L=b/a; every CP map preserves it, and after conditioning on any nonzero outcome the normalized output trace distance is at most L^2-1, independent of event probability. For direct lower Taylor weights a=1-delta,b=1.
quantifiers: Finite N; rho=sum_k p_k |D_k><D_k| and sigma=sum_k q_k |D_k><D_k| with p_k,q_k>0 and raw g_k/f_k in [a,b], 0<a<=b; any finite-dimensional CP trace-nonincreasing map Phi; P=Tr Phi(rho)>0. The direct explicit-weight instance uses f_k=exp(-(k-N/2)^2/N), 0<delta<1, and a=1-delta,b=1.
proof: Normalization gives G/F as a p-weighted average in [a,b], hence q_k/p_k in [a/b,b/a]. Both states vanish outside the same symmetric subspace, so L^-1 rho<=sigma<=L rho on the whole Hilbert space. CP order preservation and normalization imply L^-2 tau<=upsilon<=L^2 tau, whence D(tau,upsilon)<=L^2-1 by the positive-part trace bound. Full proof in RESULT.txt section 3.
cost: The order lemma has no CP-map cost claim. With direct rational Taylor weights, delta=eps/16 for rational 0<eps<=1/2 gives conditional trace distance at most 128 eps/961, for every N. The direct weight construction and bit sizes are charged in RESULT.txt section 2; no Cycle-3 premise is used.
source_boundary: This is an internally proved generic relative-order stability lemma instantiated by explicit direct rational weights. It does not imply that arbitrary CP maps are classically simulable and does not rely on N125/Cycle-3.

claim: For an open-boundary rational 1D MPO Kraus operator K with supplied TNI promise and bond chi, conditional computational-basis output sampling for K sigma K* can be performed with exact rational contractions and finite-bit sequential rounding in time polynomial in N, chi, local coefficient bit lengths, and log(1/epsilon), with exact zero-event detection and no 1/P runtime factor. For the explicit Gaussian-sector target, directly constructed rational weights give total conditional output distance below 0.259 epsilon.
quantifiers: N-qubit target rho=sum_k f_k/F |D_k><D_k|, f_k=exp(-(k-N/2)^2/N); direct relative rational weights at delta=epsilon/16 for rational 0<epsilon<=1/2; K is a supplied length-N open-boundary rational MPO, maximum bond chi, local entry bit bound B, and promised K*K<=I; output is computational-basis measurement after K-success conditioning.
proof: The direct weights define an exactly rational Dicke-diagonal MPO with ket/bra count-pair bond (N+1)^2. K sigma K* has bond at most M=(N+1)^2 chi^2. Exact prefix/suffix rational contractions produce branch masses and decide zero success; dyadic branch thresholds contribute at most epsilon/8 TV. The direct relative-order CP bound contributes at most 128 epsilon/961, for total below 0.259 epsilon. Complete proof in RESULT.txt section 3.
cost: Set M=(N+1)^2 chi^2. MPO formation and N-step prefix sampling use O(N M^2) rational operations. Direct weights use r=O(N), m=O(1+log(N/epsilon)); their normalized MPO entries have conservative bit height B_sigma=O(N^2 m(log N+log m)+N). With B_loc=O(M^2(B+B_sigma+1)), contraction height H=O(N(B_loc+log(2M))); schoolbook bit work O(N M^2 H^2), plus polynomial-time denominator bookkeeping. Random bits O(N log(N/epsilon)). The exact success mass bit length is included; no numeric 1/P factor appears.

The internal result is the explicit direct-weight relative-order guarantee plus this supplied MPO sampler; it does not use N125/Cycle-3, does not verify K*K<=I, and covers neither arbitrary quantum circuits nor global POVMs. N118/N123 overlap remains unresolved/source-reported.

claim: For every N>=1 and rational 0<delta<1, the explicit Gaussian-sector weights f_k=exp(-(k-N/2)^2/N) admit deterministic positive rational approximants g_k with (1-delta)f_k<=g_k<=f_k and polynomial construction time/bit size in N and the encoded delta.
quantifiers: N>=1 integer, k=0,...,N, rational delta in (0,1). Let u_k=(2k-N)^2/(4N), r_k be the least power of two >=1+u_k, v_k=u_k/r_k, and m_k the least odd integer with 2^m_k>=6r_k/delta.
proof: Set g_k=(sum_{j=0}^{m_k}(-v_k)^j/j!)^{r_k}. The odd Taylor partial sum lower-bounds e^-v, the next even sum upper-bounds it, and their gap is at most 2^-m. Since e^-v>1/3, the lower/upper ratio is at least 1-delta/(2r). Raising to r and using Bernoulli gives g_k/e^-u>=1-delta; the upper inequality follows from the lower Taylor bound. Positivity follows from the same alternating-series bound. Full derivation in RESULT.txt section 2.
cost: r_k=O(N), m_k=O(1+log(N/delta)); each g_k numerator and denominator has O(N m_k(log N+log(m_k+1))) bits. Horner evaluation plus repeated squaring constructs all N+1 weights in deterministic polynomial bit time. A conservative normalized weight/MPO-entry bound is B_sigma=O(N^2 m_*(log N+log(m_*+1))+N), m_*=max_k m_k.
source_boundary: Elementary alternating Taylor bounds and rational arithmetic; no external theorem, N125, or Cycle-3 premise. This is a matched baseline, not a novelty claim.
falsifier: Any exact rational fixture violating positivity or the proved lower/upper bracket; the executable verifier checks finite fixtures only.
evidence: consumer_gate/verify_direct_relative.py: exact Fraction brackets on all k for N=1,2,4,8,20 at delta=1/16. This is finite corroboration; general guarantee follows from the analytic proof.

claim: In the pair-local bilinear model for computing the supplied entries (XY)_ij, the exact multiplication-gate minimum is |W|D over every field.
quantifiers: Any field F, X in F^(N×D), Y in F^(D×N), supplied mask W with m distinct ordered pairs. Each multiplication gate is a product of one row-supported linear form and one column-supported linear form assigned to one output pair; linear preprocessing/decoding are unrestricted.
proof: Project the decoded z_ij onto the disjoint monomial space span{x_ik y_lj}; its coefficient matrix is I_D. Each gate assigned to (i,j) contributes a rank-one matrix, so at least D gates are needed per pair. The direct algorithm attains mD.
cost: Exact scalar multiplication count mD in the specified model. At D=N^(1/4), m=Theta(N^(15/8)), this is Theta(N^(17/8)); outside the model no lower bound follows.
baseline: Direct selected dot products. A seven-product Strassen identity for 2x2 full multiplication is an exact mixed-support escape.
falsifier: A circuit in the stated pair-local model with fewer than mD gates.

claim: A supplied exact rational Laurent witness with r rank-one summands and factor exponents in [-d,d] gives rank_Q(T^tensor m)<=r^m(2md+1)^2 by exact constant-coefficient extraction, with explicit coefficient and dense-output costs.

proof: Expand G(t)^tensor m and take its constant coefficient. For each choice of one of r summands in each copy, choose two factor exponents u,v; the third exponent is forced to -u-v, yielding at most (2md+1)^2 simple tensors.
cost: Output-sensitive and generally exponential in m; coefficient heights, verification, and represented extension descent are recorded in the child result.
